newsitem.title: JAPAN: Minor Metals - Rhodium pushed higher by other PGMs.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals - Rhodium pushed higher by other PGMs.

text.p: The price of rhodium has surged in tandem with other platinum group metals (PGMs), which were pushed up by a five-month absence of Russian supplies from the market, minor metals traders said on Tuesday.

"Rhodium users are buying the metal as they saw prices of other white metals such as platinum and palladium soaring," said one trader. "Demand in Japan is set to rise this year as we've seen good car sales."
Traders said the metal, mainly used in catalytic converters for cars, was quoted at $390-$400 an ounce on Tuesday in Asia, well above levels around $300 seen in London last Thursday.
Russian exports of PGMs, which include platinum, palladium and rhodium, are expected to resume in late June or early July.

Some traders attributed the sharp rise in rhodium prices to moves by U.S. speculators, who were also seen behind the surge in palladium and platinum prices, although others said it was unlikely that speculators would buy rhodium.
Traders agreed that, while the metal's price might rise further, current price levels would not dampen Japan's demand, which stands around two tonnes per year, in view of strong car sales.
"The market is tight as we haven't seen any Russian supplies since February, but there must have been a lot of metal bought in the past," added another trader.
In the cobalt market, prices eased further as traders expect the U.S. government to resume stockpile sales following a court ruling expected on Friday.

"The focus is back on the DLA (Defense Logistics Agency) again. Now we are waiting for the DLA's review of its sales plan for this year. They can't be planning to sell all of the remaining 1,800 tonnes by September," said one trader.
High-grade cobalt was quoted at $23.50-24.50 a pound, while low-grade cobalt eased to $19.00-21.00 amid talk of abundant offers for Russian cobalt.
Domestic Chinese prices were also said to be softening to around 435,000 yuan ($52,457) to 440,000 yuan per tonne, down from about 460,000 yuan to 470,000 yuan per tonne in April.
"Prices are softening in response to the world market," said one China-based trader, noting that Russian material was pressuring global prices.

One source reported business concluded for cobalt ingots at $20.50 per pound, CIF Hong Kong or Shantou (a south China port), but others said that cobalt ingots were trading between $20.75 and $21.75 per pound.
In Hong Kong, dealers said bismuth continued enjoying a flurry of trade, with deals heard done at just below $4.00 per pound and Chinese offers still hovering above $4.00 per pound.
In the Japanese magnesium market, prices remained firm at $2,300/2,600 per tonne.
Traders expect Japanese demand to ease in the third quarter as beverage can makers would have produced enough cans to meet summer demand by then.
Price negotiations on third-quarter supplies between traders and end-users started this week.
"Now we have to see how much of a rise in prices users will accept in the talks starting this week," said one trader.

While the metal's dollar-denominated price has seen a steady increase over the last several months, the dollar's retreat against the yen has made it difficult for suppliers to push for a rise in yen-based prices, traders said.
-- Nao Nakanishi, Tokyo commodities desk +81-3-3432-7431
